clinician.trajectory_summary: A 68-year-old man presented with one month of hypogastric and right lower quadrant discomfort and colicky pain radiating to the back, accompanied by weight loss and anorexia. Abdominal CT demonstrated a well-demarcated homogeneous solitary cecal mass with ileum wall thickening. There was no association of pain with defecation or eating. Histopathology of the biopsy showed lamina propria infiltration by polymorphonuclear cells and eosinophils with immunohistochemical positivity for vimentin, CD68, focal ALK and SMA, negative for c-Kit and CD34, supporting IMT diagnosis. Following pathological confirmation, the patient was referred for surgery to remove the mass.
